conventions.testing: Unit tests in mod tests blocks with tree-sitter parsing verification
conventions.linting: clippy with deny-level rules for undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used
conventions.error_handling: Option/Result patterns with expect/unwrap in tests, tracing for errors

patterns: Language registration via mod.rs match arms in get_language_info() and get_ts_language()
Query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, etc.) defined as pub const in language-specific modules
Handler functions (extract_function_name, extract_inheritance) defined per language
Unconditional dependency in core crate Cargo.toml (no feature flags)
constraints: DEFUSE_QUERY is required - LanguageInfo.defuse_query is a mandatory field
No feature flags - all languages unconditionally compiled in
tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 has tree-sitter-language ^0.1.0 as normal dep, tree-sitter as dev-only
test_coverage: Each language module has unit tests for element queries, inheritance extraction, and defuse sites. Java has comprehensive tests for extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance, and defuse_query.

library_findings.notes: alex-pinkus/tree-sitter-swift; dev-only tree-sitter dependency avoids version conflict

approaches.name: Follow java.rs pattern
approaches.description: Create swift.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY constants and extract_inheritance handler. Wire into mod.rs and lang.rs following css/java patterns.
cons: Requires careful query crafting for Swift-specific node kinds

approaches.name: Minimal stub approach
approaches.description: Create minimal swift.rs with only ELEMENT_QUERY and DEFUSE_QUERY, skip handlers initially.

recommendation: Follow java.rs pattern - it provides complete feature coverage with tested patterns, ensuring Swift support is production-ready from the start.

inheritance_walk_citation: From alex-pinkus/tree-sitter-swift grammar: Walk inheritance_specifier descendants; for each, read the inherits_from field, then find the type_identifier or user_type text to get the name. Multiple specifiers are siblings under _inheritance_specifiers (comma-separated in source).
